clue.text: Positioned in the centre, as one really is

definitions.meaning: literally placed at the core or middle of something
idiom for in one's true nature, deep down

explanation.surface: A description of someone placed centrally who is also being their true self.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally (located at the core) and idiomatically (fundamentally, in one's real nature).

clue.text: Like amount editor cut, it's fake

parts.note: like, as in 'as' meaning similar to
an amount or total is a sum
the word editor cut short leaves the usual abbreviation ED

explanation.surface: A magazine total trimmed by the editor turns out to be a bogus figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumed name or manner is a false, put-on one, so fake is a synonym.

clue.text: What's needed, specially in unethical NHS era?

definitions.text: What's needed, specially in unethical NHS era?

indicators.note: specially here means made specially, so the letters that follow are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what people must have when the National Health Service is going through a dubious period.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's free National Health Service; the whole clue doubles as a definition, suggesting private cover is what you would need if it became untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Private medical cover is what someone would need if the state health service could not be trusted.

clue.text: Early in the day, employ workers with little time for play

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning hours
to employ something is to use it
workers can be called men
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Advice to hire a workforce in the morning while leaving them no break for recreation.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement and play both mean recreation or entertainment.

clue.text: Steady paces shown by left-wingers

definitions.meaning: a horse's gait between walking and cantering, done steadily
informal shortening for Trotskyists, followers of Leon Trotsky

explanation.surface: Horses moving at an even gait are displayed by socialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a jogging gait, and also slang for Trotskyist radicals on the political left.

clue.text: Coach without covering one book

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: minus means without, as in 'minus his hat'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A trainer arrives without even one volume to cover the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a passenger vehicle, and a small bus is one kind.

clue.text: Extremely mature elm, rotten at the bottom

indicators.note: rotten suggests the letters of the tree's name have decayed into disorder

parts.note: something at the very bottom is in the lowest position

explanation.surface: An ancient elm tree that has gone rotten at its base.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellow means ripe or matured, and the superlative form means most matured.

clue.text: Old gold coin, not common

definitions.meaning: a medieval English gold coin worth a third of a pound
aristocratic, not of the commoner class

explanation.surface: An antique gold piece that is described as rare.
explanation.walkthrough: The old English coin of this name was gold, first struck under Edward III.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both a historic English coin and the aristocracy, as opposed to commoners.

clue.text: Decorations provided on the occasion of a party?

definitions.text: Decorations provided on the occasion of a party?

parts.words: Decorations provided on the occasion of a party?
parts.note: reads as balloons and streamers for a celebration, but means British awards announced each year on the monarch's official anniversary

explanation.surface: Bunting and balloons put up for someone's celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, knighthoods and medals are announced twice a year, once at New Year and once on the sovereign's official birthday in June.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of British state awards published to mark the sovereign's official birthday.

clue.text: Corrupt us lawyer removed from courts hysterically

indicators.note: removed from says the answer is extracted from within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dishonest American attorney is dragged out of court screaming.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for an unscrupulous lawyer who uses shady methods.

clue.text: French sculpture erected in us for free

definitions.text: French sculpture erected in us for free

parts.words: French sculpture erected in us for free
parts.note: reads as a gift of art set up at no charge, but describes the copper monument given by France and standing in New York harbour as a symbol of freedom

explanation.surface: A piece of French art put up in America without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York monument designed by Bartholdi was a gift from France and symbolises freedom.

clue.text: It's said to be a device for measuring distance

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a gauge such as a gas or parking meter

explanation.surface: A definition of a gauge used to measure how far things are.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic SI unit of length, roughly 39 inches, so a distance.

clue.text: Songbird adapted to a nest outside church

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters sit around the other piece
adapted means the letters of the phrase are altered into another form

explanation.surface: A bird modifies its nest built outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small chat-type bird whose call sounds like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Make very obvious trip back to base

definitions.meaning: to make a point forcefully understood
a journey by car to one's house

explanation.surface: Emphasising a point, and also travelling back to headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for emphasising a point until it lands, and literally a car journey to where you live.

clue.text: In awkward position, immediately right there

definitions.meaning: put in a difficult situation, required to answer
at the very scene of events

explanation.surface: Someone in a tricky spot, needing to act this instant at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom covering being put in a tight corner, acting at once, and being at the scene itself.

clue.text: Piece of furniture one sits in daily

indicators.note: sits in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner, also called a char or charwoman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Describing the item a person sits in every day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' or 'char' is a domestic cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat for one person with a back is a common piece of furniture.

clue.text: Very serious foreign article in journal

parts.note: chronic in British informal use means very bad or serious
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A grave piece from overseas published in a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record or account, like a journal.

clue.text: Attack where shooting happens

definitions.meaning: an assault or the start of hostilities
on a film set, where scenes are shot

explanation.surface: An assault at the place where guns are fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means an assault or beginning, and filming takes place on a set.

clue.text: Services provided by government departments

definitions.meaning: religious ceremonies or acts of help
ministries such as the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Help supplied by ministries of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious services and kindly acts are called offices, as are ministries such as the Home Office.

clue.text: Teaching position arranged in trip south

indicators.note: arranged means the letters given are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A teaching job organised during a journey southwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor's post is a role in teaching.

clue.text: Pupils having arrived initially at school in carriage

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren turn up at their school in a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is Eton College, the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Strip cut from forest yielding free bark I distributed

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread out and shared into a new order

explanation.surface: Clearing woodland yields loose bark which someone hands round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleared strip in woodland made to stop a fire spreading.

clue.text: High-pitched signal getting British former PM up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: Robert Peel was a 19th-century Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A shrill alert summons an ex-premier from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A short shrill electronic tone, as from a pager.

clue.text: Whip producing nothing audible

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A lash that makes no sound.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing; the K of the Russian lash is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian lash formerly used for flogging criminals.

clue.text: Master of concealment, part of tradition in Japan

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An expert at hiding is part of Japanese custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal Japanese covert agents were trained in stealth and disguise.

clue.text: Lack of respect from those around monarch creates offence

definitions.text: Lack of respect from those around monarch
definitions.meaning: disdain shown by the royal entourage, a court being a sovereign's attendants
a legal wrong of disobeying or disrespecting a judge

explanation.surface: Disdain among the royal entourage leads to resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally scorn felt by a royal household, and legally the crime of defying a judge.

clue.text: Crest drops water on turning vessel

indicators.note: turning means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: the crest of a hill is its top
to drop water on something wets it

explanation.surface: A wave crest crashes over a boat as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cooking pot used for slow-cooking stews, so a vessel.

clue.text: Time and motive for a serious crime

parts.note: a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: Investigating when and why a grave offence was committed.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is a grave offence.
